speaker: Art Bell
text: From the high desert and the great American Southwest…

source.title: The Truth Was Out There: On the Legacy of Art Bell, Los Angeles Review of Books
source.supports: Quotes the sign-on: "From the high desert and the great American Southwest," Bell intoned over the pulse of Giorgio Moroder's paranoid instrumental.

text: On a night of open lines with a line set aside for Area 51 insiders, a frantic caller, audibly crying, warned that they would triangulate his position really soon. During his call the satellite uplink failed and the show went silent.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Open Lines with Area 51 Employees

source.title: The Truth Was Out There: On the Legacy of Art Bell, Los Angeles Review of Books
source.supports: Dates the call to September 11, 1997, with lines open and a line for Area 51 informants; the caller was "audibly crying", said "They'll triangulate on this position really, really soon", was cut off mid-sentence, and "The satellite uplink transmitter had failed without explanation."

text: Rocket scientist David Adair talked with Art about UFOs and Area 51.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Area 51 and UFO Technology

source.title: Rebroadcast: David Adair, Coast to Coast AM (aired 2006-01-08)
source.supports: "In this rebroadcast from 11/17/97, Art Bell spoke with rocket scientist David Adair on UFOs and Area 51."

text: Courtney Brown joined Art and Chuck Shramek, whose new photograph of Comet Hale-Bopp seemed to show a bright object near it.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Remote Viewing the Hale-Bopp Anomaly

source.title: Exposing PseudoAstronomy, Chuck Shramek (Stuart Robbins); see also Wikipedia, Comet Hale-Bopp, UFO claims
source.supports: Robbins: "I realized early in the episode (November 14, 1996) that I was listening to THE interview that started the whole thing", and Courtney Brown "and his remote viewing claims". Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comet_Hale%E2%80%93Bopp#UFO_claims): Shramek photographed an object near the comet and called Coast to Coast AM to report a "Saturn-like object"; Brown concluded a spacecraft was trailing it.

text: Art and Whitley Strieber talked with Courtney Brown about the Hale-Bopp companion photo, which astronomers showed was an altered copy of one of their own comet images.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Whitley Strieber and the Courtney Brown Controversy

source.title: Exposing PseudoAstronomy, Chuck Shramek (Stuart Robbins); see also Wikipedia, Comet Hale-Bopp, UFO claims
source.supports: Robbins: Brown "provided the hoaxed photographs to Art Bell and Whitley Strieber". Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comet_Hale%E2%80%93Bopp#UFO_claims): Hainaut and Tholen revealed "the alleged photo was an altered copy of one of their own comet images".

text: Mel Waters first came on the show to describe a hole on his land in Washington State that seemed to have no bottom. He said he had lowered miles of fishing line into it without reaching anything.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Contact and Disclosure with Dr. Steven Greer, Mel Waters First Appearance

source.title: Mel's Hole, Wikipedia
source.supports: "The legend of the bottomless hole started on February 21, 1997, when a man identifying himself as Mel Waters appeared as a guest on Coast to Coast AM"; rural property in Kittitas County, Washington; no bottom "by the time 80,000 feet (15 mi; 24 km) of line had been used."

text: Mel Waters came back with an update on his bottomless hole, and described a second hole he was investigating.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Mel's Hole Returns

source.title: The Return of Mel's Hole, Coast to Coast AM (original air date January 29, 2002)
source.supports: "Mel Waters returned with an update on the 'bottomless hole' on his property... He described a second hole that he was investigating."

text: Dr. Steven Greer on the beginnings of his Disclosure Project.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Contact and Disclosure with Dr. Steven Greer, Mel Waters First Appearance

source.title: Art Bell: Somewhere in Time, Coast to Coast AM (2025-09-27)
source.supports: "returned to February 21, 1997, when Dr. Steven Greer discussed the beginnings of the Disclosure Project, and Mel Waters of 'Mel's Hole' shared an update."

text: The night of the Phoenix Lights, dozens of frantic callers told Art of a very busy night in the skies above Arizona. One was Peter Davenport of the National UFO Reporting Center.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - The Phoenix Lights (First Night Coverage) with Peter Davenport & Sean David Morton

source.title: Phoenix Lights UFO sightings in 1997: An oral history, Phoenix New Times (2025-03-13)
source.supports: On the night of March 13, 1997, "On that night's episode of... 'Coast to Coast AM,' the late Art Bell fielded dozens of 'frantic' callers describing 'a very busy night in the skies above Arizona.' One was from NUFORC director Peter Davenport."

text: Steven Gibbs on the time machine he said he had invented, one he claimed would let a person physically visit any time in the past or future.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Time Travel Technology

source.title: Inventing a Time Machine, Coast to Coast AM (original air date January 13, 1997)
source.supports: "Steven Gibbs... talked about his claims of inventing a time machine that would allow users to physically visit any time in the past or future."

text: Professor Michio Kaku joins Art for the first time, on how our Type Zero civilization might reach Type One status when we harvest the true power of the planet.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Theoretical Physics

source.title: Art Bell: Somewhere in Time, Coast to Coast AM, 2021-08-21
source.supports: Date, person and topic: "Art Bell: Somewhere in Time returned to 8/22/97, when professor Michio Kaku joined Art for the first time to speculate on how our Type Zero civilization might reach Type One status".

text: Terence McKenna on the nature of time, which he likened to a constant struggle between habit and novelty.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - TimeWave Zero

source.title: Art Bell Vault: Remote Viewing Predictions / End of Time & Psychedelics, Coast to Coast AM, 2025-02-26
source.supports: Dates the McKenna show to 5/22/1997 and says he spoke on "the nature of time, which he likened to a constant struggle between 'habit and novelty.'"

text: New Year's Eve 1999: Art marked the change of the millennium and addressed fears about whether or not Y2K would cause huge problems worldwide.

source.title: New Year's Eve 1999, Coast to Coast AM show page (Friday, December 31, 1999)
source.supports: Date and event: "In Art Bell's New Year's Eve 1999 special, he marked the change of the millennium, and addressed fears about whether or not Y2K would cause huge problems worldwide."

text: Major Ed Dames joins Art to discuss remote viewing as well as many black op projects.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Remote Viewing

source.title: Art Bell: Somewhere in Time, Coast to Coast AM, 2009-04-11 (the source data/notable.md already uses)
source.supports: Date, person and topic: replays "12/7/95" with "Maj. Ed Dames"; "They discussed remote viewing as well as many black op projects."

text: The Killshot: Ed Dames's long-running prediction of a series of solar flares that he and his remote viewing team believed would hit Earth, causing great destruction and death.

source.title: Major Ed Dames, Coast to Coast AM guest page
source.supports: July 17, 2004 'The Killshot': "a series of solar flares that he and his remote viewing research team believe will hit earth causing an extreme amount of destruction and death"; it is still discussed in 2011, 2012 and 2019 entries (long-running).

text: Art and Whitley Strieber wrote The Coming Global Superstorm together. It became the basis for the film The Day After Tomorrow.

source.title: The Coming Global Superstorm, Wikipedia
source.supports: "a 1999 book by Art Bell and Whitley Strieber" whose scenarios "were the basis of the 2004 science fiction film The Day After Tomorrow."

text: Art became a licensed amateur radio operator at 13. His call sign was W6OBB.

source.title: Art Bell, Wikipedia
source.supports: "at the age of 13, he became a licensed amateur radio operator"; "His call sign was W6OBB."

text: Before talk radio, Art was a disc jockey in Okinawa, where he was said to have set a record for continuous broadcasting, 116 hours and 15 minutes, to raise money to ferry stranded Vietnamese orphans to the United States.

source.title: Art Bell, Radio Host Who Tuned In to the Dark Side, Dies at 72, Sam Roberts, New York Times (via WRAL), 2018-04-17
source.supports: "a disc jockey for an English-language station in Okinawa"; "said to have set a record for continuous broadcasting, 116 hours and 15 minutes, to raise money to ferry stranded Vietnamese orphans from Saigon to the United States".

text: The show came from Art's home in Pahrump, Nevada, in the high desert west of Las Vegas.

source.title: Art Bell, Radio Host Who Tuned In to the Dark Side, Dies at 72, Sam Roberts, New York Times (via WRAL), 2018-04-17
source.supports: "From a home studio 65 miles west of Las Vegas"; "his home in Pahrump, Nevada". ARRL's obituary (arrl.org, 2018-04-14) also has him producing the show from his own studio in the High Desert of Nevada.

text: The lines had names: East of the Rockies, West of the Rockies, the Wildcard Line and the First-Time Callers line.

source.title: Art Bell turned conspiracy theories into a theater of the mind, The Outline, Michael Powell, 2018-04-28
source.supports: "one for Americans to the east of the Rockies, one for everyone to the west of the Rockies, a line for international callers, another for first-time callers, and a 'Wild Card' line".

text: Dreamland with Art Bell was his Sunday night show.

source.title: Art Bell Has Heard It All, From 'Coast To Coast', The Spokesman-Review, 1997-03-13
source.supports: Gives the schedule: "Dreamland with Art Bell" airs at 10 p.m. Sundays.

text: Coast to Coast AM opened with Chase, Giorgio Moroder's theme from Midnight Express.

source.title: Coast to Coast AM, Wikipedia
source.supports: Gives the opening theme as "Chase (Theme from Midnight Express) by Giorgio Moroder".

text: Ghost to Ghost was one of Art's yearly Halloween traditions: listeners emailed, faxed and called in with their best ghost stories.

source.title: Ghost-to-Ghost 1994, Coast to Coast AM (show page, 1994-10-28)
source.supports: "One of the first of Art's yearly Halloween traditions, listeners emailed, faxed, and called in with their best ghost stories."

text: Paranormal researcher Dr. Morgan Spence came on in 2001 to discuss the real possibilities for the existence of shadow people.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Shadow People Phenomenon

source.title: Art Bell: Somewhere in Time, Coast to Coast AM (show page, 2013-02-02)
source.supports: "returned to 5/31/01 when paranormal expert Dr. Morgan Spence discussed the real possibilities for the existence of Shadow People".

text: Gordon-Michael Scallion, the intuitive, with his predictions of major earth changes.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Earth Changes Predictions

source.title: Gordon-Michael Scallion, Coast to Coast AM guest page
source.supports: "Art Bell: Somewhere in Time returned to 9/19/97 when intuitive Gordon-Michael Scallion rocked the house with predictions of major earth changes."

text: Art's farewell in April 2000. Mike Siegel took over Coast to Coast AM, and Art was back the next year.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Art's Farewell

source.title: Art Bell, Wikipedia
source.supports: "On April 11, 2000, Mike Siegel was introduced as the new host of Coast to Coast AM, taking over on April 27" and "Bell returned to Coast to Coast AM in February 2001."

text: Art's last official show as host of Coast to Coast AM, closing out 2002 by reviewing the year's predictions and taking new ones for 2003.

episode.title: Coast to Coast AM - Art's Farewell Show with Predictions

source.title: Art's Farewell Show, Coast to Coast AM (show page, 2002-12-31)
source.supports: Art Bell's "last official show as the host of Coast to Coast", "reviewing predictions from the year 2002, and soliciting new ones for 2003."

text: George Noory took over the weeknights in January 2003. Art came back that September as a weekend host and kept it up until 2007.

source.title: Art Bell, Wikipedia
source.supports: "Bell was replaced by George Noory as weekday host of Coast to Coast AM on January 1, 2003"; "Bell returned in September 2003 as a weekend host"; on July 1, 2007 he announced his retirement from weekend hosting.

text: Midnight in the Desert, Art's return to the air in 2015, opened with Graham Hancock.

episode.title: Midnight in the Desert - Graham Hancock

source.title: Art Bell, Graham Hancock Official Website, 2015-07-20
source.supports: "Join me and Art Bell, Monday night 20 July", linking to a FAQ on "the new show, Midnight in the Desert".

text: Art stepped down from Midnight in the Desert in December 2015, citing concerns about his family's safety.

source.title: Art Bell, Wikipedia
source.supports: "On December 11, 2015, Bell permanently stepped down as host of Midnight in the Desert due to concerns about his family's safety", after armed trespassers fired gunshots on his property.
